## Code Review

This pull request updates the handling of zero-output worker launches by transitioning from a 'needs-brief-rewrite' hold to a 'dispatch-infrastructure-failure' hold, ensuring that infrastructure issues are diagnosed before re-dispatching. It also introduces a recovery mechanism in the reconciliation script to requeue issues that were stranded by stale labels. Feedback was provided to simplify the `jq` filtering logic for better maintainability and to remove redundant label removal flags in the reconciliation loop, as those labels are already guaranteed to be absent by the selection criteria.

## Code Review

This pull request updates the agent documentation and git workflow to allow an exception for running release and version-manager commands directly on the main branch, provided changes are merged and verified. The review feedback suggests enhancing these updates with technical reasoning—specifically regarding how the Edit tool tracks absolute paths—and adding warnings about the risks of destroying active worktrees to ensure better agent compliance and safety.

## Code Review

This pull request implements a daemon-safe shim for the OpenCode CLI to ensure consistent execution in systemd environments by decoupling it from shell-based Node managers. Key changes include the generation of a wrapper script in `~/.local/bin`, localized `PATH` management, and automated clearing of stale canary caches. Review feedback identifies high-severity security risks regarding untrusted search paths (CWE-426) in the `PATH` construction and recommends improving the robustness of file write operations.

<details>
<summary>I am having trouble creating individual review comments. Click here to see my feedback.</summary>

### .agents/scripts/setup/_services.sh (129-130)

![security-high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/security-high-priority.svg) ![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The current `PATH` construction can lead to a security vulnerability (CWE-426) if `bin_dir` is empty or resolves to a dot (`.`). In POSIX shell, an empty component in `PATH` (like a leading colon or double colons) is interpreted as the current directory. Since this path is used in a daemon/shim context, it should only contain absolute, trusted directories. Additionally, add a guard clause to check if the variable is empty before use and avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` to ensure diagnostic information is visible.

```suggestion
	bin_dir=""; [[ -n "$bin" ]] && bin_dir=$(dirname "$bin" || printf '')
	[[ "$bin_dir" == "." ]] && bin_dir=""
	path_value="${bin_dir:+$bin_dir:}${HOME}/.local/bin:${HOME}/.aidevops/agents/scripts:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"
```

<summary>References</summary>

1. In shell scripts, add guard clauses to check if a variable is empty before using it, especially when its value is derived from an external command.
2. Avoid suppressing stderr with '2>/dev/null' to ensure that diagnostic information is visible.

![security-high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/security-high-priority.svg) ![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

This is interpreted as the current directory (`.`), which is a security risk in a daemon environment. The path construction should be guarded to ensure only non-empty, absolute directories are added. Also, avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` to maintain visibility of diagnostic information.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a shim to normalize labels for tracking issues created via raw `gh issue create` commands, ensuring they include appropriate origin, status, and type labels when specific title patterns are detected. The changes include documentation updates, the implementation of several helper functions in the `gh` script, and new test cases. Review feedback suggests improving the robustness of the shell functions by using `local IFS` and `read -ra` to avoid globbing and side effects, as well as extending title flag support to include the `-t` short flag and correctly handling multiple flag occurrences.

<details>
<summary>I am having trouble creating individual review comments. Click here to see my feedback.</summary>

### .agents/scripts/gh (816-832)

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The function `_shim_arg_labels_contain` modifies the global `IFS` variable and manually restores it. It is safer to use `local IFS` to avoid side effects if the function is interrupted. Additionally, the `for label in $labels` loop is vulnerable to globbing if a label contains characters like `*` or `?`. Using `read -ra` with a here-string is a more robust way to split the comma-separated string without globbing in Bash.

```
_shim_arg_labels_contain() {
	local labels="$1"
	local needle="$2"
	local label=""
	local label_array
	local IFS=,
	read -ra label_array <<< "$labels"
	for label in "${label_array[@]}"; do
		label="${label#"${label%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
		label="${label%"${label##*[![:space:]]}"}"
		if [[ "$label" == "$needle" ]]; then
			return 0
		fi
	done
	return 1
}
```

### .agents/scripts/gh (834-850)

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Similar to `_shim_arg_labels_contain`, this function should use `local IFS` and avoid globbing during word splitting. Using `read -ra` is recommended for safety and clarity.

```
_shim_arg_labels_have_prefix() {
	local labels="$1"
	local prefix="$2"
	local label=""
	local label_array
	local IFS=,
	read -ra label_array <<< "$labels"
	for label in "${label_array[@]}"; do
		label="${label#"${label%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
		label="${label%"${label##*[![:space:]]}"}"
		if [[ "$label" == "${prefix}"* ]]; then
			return 0
		fi
	done
	return 1
}
```

### .agents/scripts/gh (852-870)

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `_shim_issue_create_get_title` function is missing support for the `-t` short flag, which is commonly used in interactive sessions. Additionally, it currently returns the first title found, whereas `gh` typically respects the last occurrence of a flag. The suggested implementation handles both short flags (including attached values like `-tTitle`) and ensures the last title wins.

```
_shim_issue_create_get_title() {
	local idx=0
	local arg=""
	local title=""
	local found=1
	while [[ $idx -lt ${#_modified_args[@]} ]]; do
		arg="${_modified_args[$idx]}"
		case "$arg" in
		--title | -t)
			title="${_modified_args[idx + 1]:-}"
			found=0
			idx=$((idx + 1))
			;;
		--title=*)
			title="${arg#--title=}"
			found=0
			;;
		-t*)
			title="${arg#-t}"
			found=0
			;;
		esac
		idx=$((idx + 1))
	done
	[[ $found -eq 0 ]] && printf '%s\n' "$title"
	return $found
}
```

</details>

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a mechanism to handle "orphan" dispatch claims—claims that exceed a grace period without an assignee or worker launch evidence—preventing them from blocking future dispatches. Key changes include the addition of _filter_orphan_prelaunch_claims and _filter_claims_with_launch_evidence functions, the DISPATCH_CLAIM_ORPHAN_GRACE configuration variable, and new unit tests. A review comment suggests an optimization to skip the GitHub API call in _filter_orphan_prelaunch_claims if all claims are still within the grace period.

<details>
<summary>I am having trouble creating individual review comments. Click here to see my feedback.</summary>

### .agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh (534-543)

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `gh api` call to fetch issue details is performed for every call to `_fetch_claims` when active claims are present. This can be optimized by skipping the API call if all current claims are still fresh. Additionally, when checking for assignees, if none are found, the logic should allow for recovery by assuming the task is local, consistent with repository rules for handling malformed claims.

```suggestion
	# Optimization: skip API call if all claims are fresh.
	if ! printf '%s' "$parsed_claims" | jq -e --argjson grace "$DISPATCH_CLAIM_ORPHAN_GRACE" 'any(.age_seconds > $grace)' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		printf '%s' "$parsed_claims"
		return 0
	fi

	local assignee_count
	assignee_count=$(gh api "repos/${repo_slug}/issues/${issue_number}" --jq '.assignees | length' 2>/dev/null) || {
		printf '%s' "$parsed_claims"
		return 0
	}
	[[ "$assignee_count" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || assignee_count=0
	if [[ "$assignee_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
		printf '%s' "$parsed_claims"
		return 0
	fi
```

## Code Review

This pull request enhances the pulse-merge process by integrating GitHub repository rulesets into the required status check verification logic. It introduces helpers to fetch and match ruleset-based required contexts, supplementing classic branch protection and ensuring correct enforcement even when the classic API returns a 404. The test suite has been significantly updated to cover ruleset scenarios and now enforces that pending required checks block merges until they successfully conclude. Review feedback identifies opportunities to improve glob pattern matching, handle ruleset exclusion patterns, optimize API efficiency by avoiding N+1 queries, and deduplicate the final list of required contexts.

<details>
<summary>I am having trouble creating individual review comments. Click here to see my feedback.</summary>

### .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh (970-979)

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The glob detection pattern `refs/heads/*\**)` is overly restrictive. It only matches patterns that start with `refs/heads/` and contain an asterisk. However, GitHub rulesets also support simple globs like `*` (which matches all refs) or patterns that don't start with the full ref prefix. These would currently be ignored by the matching logic. Ensure that any fix is applied consistently to similar patterns throughout the file, and that the `$default_ref` is determined using a robust fallback mechanism.

```suggestion
	case "$pattern" in
	*"*"*)
		# shellcheck disable=SC2254 # Intentionally treat ruleset branch globs as patterns.
		case "$default_ref" in
		$pattern)
			return 0
			;;
		esac
		;;
	esac
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When applying a fix for a specific pattern, also fix other instances of the same pattern in the file for consistency.
2. To make git operations in scripts more robust, dynamically and explicitly determine the default branch instead of relying on the current checkout.
</details>

### .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh (1028-1042)

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The current implementation only evaluates `include` patterns for rulesets. GitHub repository rulesets also support `exclude` patterns, which take precedence over inclusions. If the default branch matches an exclusion pattern, the ruleset should not be applied. You should fetch and check `exclude` patterns as well. Note that while exclusion lists can vary by function purpose, for ruleset enforcement, both must be considered.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

This loop performs an individual API call for every active ruleset, leading to an N+1 query problem. For repositories with many rulesets, this could significantly slow down the merge process and consume API rate limits. Consider using a single GraphQL query to fetch all rulesets with their associated conditions and rules in one request to improve efficiency.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

		[[ -n "$ruleset_contexts" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$ruleset_contexts"

## Code Review

This pull request modifies the `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` function to prioritize circuit breaker trip detection over actor validation, ensuring breaker markers are authoritative regardless of the account that applied them. A new test case was added to verify this logic. A critical issue was identified where the lack of the `--slurp` flag in the paginated GitHub API call could lead to malformed data and incorrect auto-approvals for issues with long timelines.

<details>
<summary>I am having trouble creating individual review comments. Click here to see my feedback.</summary>

### .agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh (497-498)

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The logic here relies on `nmr_at` being a single valid ISO8601 timestamp. However, the upstream `gh api` call at line 485 (in the context) lacks the `--slurp` flag. When an issue's timeline spans multiple pages, `gh api --paginate` without `--slurp` emits one JSON object per page. This causes the `jq` filter at line 486 to produce a result for each page (e.g., `null` or an empty object for pages without NMR events), resulting in `nmr_at` and `nmr_actor` containing multiple lines or trailing newlines.

This will cause `_nmr_application_is_circuit_breaker_trip` (line 498) and `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature` (line 517) to receive malformed input, causing their internal `jq` date parsing to fail. Consequently, a circuit breaker trip or a manual hold on a long-lived issue might be incorrectly classified, leading to an unsafe auto-approval. 

To fix this, the `gh api` call at line 485 should use `--slurp`, and the `jq` filter should be updated to flatten the nested array (similar to the logic used in `_nmr_application_is_circuit_breaker_trip` at line 425).

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When fetching a list of items from the GitHub API with the `gh` command, use the `--paginate` flag to ensure all items are retrieved, not just the first page.
</details>

</details>
